## Step 1 — Confirm escalated perspectives

Escalated for deep review:
- **Keyboard & Motor Access**: MEDIUM
- **Screen Reader & Semantic Structure**: HIGH
- **Cognitive & Neurodivergent**: MEDIUM

Perspectives at LOW (not reviewed): Magnification & Reflow, Environmental Contrast, Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity, Auditory Access.

---

## Step 2 & 3 — Reference files & artifact loaded

Loaded JTBD checklists for the three escalated perspectives and ARRM routing mapping. Reviewed component markup, CSS, and interaction logic.

---

## Step 4 & 5 — Per-Perspective Checklist Execution & Findings

### Perspective: Keyboard & Motor Access (MEDIUM)
**JTBD Checklist Results:**
- [PASS] All interactive elements (`<button>`, `<a>`) reachable/operable by keyboard alone (2.1.1)
- [PASS] No keyboard traps; Tab/Shift+Tab moves focus logically through headers → pagination (2.1.2, 2.4.3)
- [PASS] Focus indicator visible: `outline: 3px solid #1565c0` with `outline-offset: -3px` meets ≥2px and ≥3:1 contrast change against adjacent UI (2.4.7, 2.4.13)
- [PASS] Activation fires on up-event (`<button>` default behavior) (2.5.2)
- [PASS] Visible label matches accessible name; sort buttons contain text labels (2.5.3)
- [PASS] Interactive targets ≥ 24x24px via padding calculations (2.5.8)

**Findings:**
```
**Finding:** Sort buttons lack `aria-sort` attribute to programmatically communicate current sort key and direction. Keyboard+AT users cannot verify or announce sort state without relying on visual cues alone.
**WCAG:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
**Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure (impacts Keyboard+AT verification)
**Severity:** MAJOR
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design)
**Evidence:** JSX lines 58-63; buttons contain text/icons but no `aria-sort` or `aria-pressed` state.
**Fix:** Add `aria-sort={sortKey === col.key ? sortDir : 'none'}` to each sort button. Update icon/text accordingly.
```

### Perspective: Screen Reader & Semantic Structure (HIGH)
**JTBD Checklist Results:**
- [PASS] Landmark present: `role="region" aria-label="Employee directory"` on table wrapper (1.3.1)
- [FAIL] Table structure uses `<div>` for rows/cells instead of semantic `<table>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<th scope="col">`. Screen readers cannot navigate by column headers or announce table context. (1.3.1, 4.1.2)
- [FAIL] Pagination links use bare numbers (`{i + 1}`) as link text without contextual labels. Screen readers announce them ambiguously (e.g., "link 1"). (2.4.4)
- [FAIL] Table updates on sort/pagination are not announced to assistive technology via `aria-live` or focus management. Users relying on AT lose awareness of data changes. (4.1.3, 2.4.3)
- [PASS] DOM order matches visual reading order (1.3.2)
- [PASS] Decorative sort icon uses `aria-hidden="true"` (1.1.1)

**Findings:**
```
**Finding:** Table rows and cells are implemented as `<div>` elements instead of semantic table markup (`<table>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<th scope="col">`). Screen readers cannot recognize column headers, announce table context, or enable grid navigation.
**WCAG:** 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
**Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure
**Severity:** CRITICAL
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design)
**Evidence:** JSX lines 56-74; CSS `.table-row`, `.table-cell` classes applied to divs.
**Fix:** Replace wrapper divs with `<table>`. Map header row to `<thead><tr><th scope="col">`, data rows to `<tbody><tr><td>`. Add `scope="col"` to all `<th>` elements.
```

```
**Finding:** Pagination links use bare numbers as visible text without contextual labels. Screen readers announce them ambiguously, breaking link purpose in context.
**WCAG:** 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)
**Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure
**Severity:** MAJOR
**Route to:** Content Author (secondary: Front-End Dev)
**Evidence:** JSX lines 88-93; `aria-label` or visible text context is missing.
**Fix:** Update link text to `"Page {i + 1}"` or add `aria-label={`Go to page ${i + 1}`}`. Consider replacing `<a href="#">` with `<button type="button">` for client-side navigation.
```

```
**Finding:** Table data updates (sort/pagination) are not announced to assistive technology. No `aria-live` region or focus management is triggered when state changes.
**WCAG:** 4.1.3 Status Messages; 2.4.3 Focus Order
**Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure
**Severity:** MAJOR
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (secondary: UX Design)
**Evidence:** Component state updates (`page`, `sortKey`) trigger re-render but no live region or focus shift is implemented.
**Fix:** Wrap the table data area in `<div aria-live="polite" role="status">` or add a dedicated status div outside the table that updates with `"Showing page X of Y"`. Manage focus to the table wrapper on sort/pagination change.
```

### Perspective: Cognitive & Neurodivergent (MEDIUM)
**JTBD Checklist Results:**
- [PASS] Layout is predictable; main content in expected location; no layout shifts on interaction.
- [PASS] Visual hierarchy clear; headings/grouping guide reading order.
- [PASS] No autoplay media or unprompted modals.
- [MINOR] Sorting resets pagination to page 0 without warning or announcement. Users may lose their place if they were reviewing later pages. (3.2.1, 3.3.4)
- [PASS] Content avoids jargon; labels are plain and consistent.

**Findings:**
```
**Finding:** Sorting a column silently resets pagination to page 0 without warning or announcement. Users may lose their place or miss data they were reviewing on subsequent pages.
**WCAG:** 3.2.1 On Focus (context change); 3.3.4 Error Prevention
**Perspective:** Cognitive & Neurodivergent
**Severity:** MINOR
**Route to:** UX Design (secondary: Front-End Dev)
**Evidence:** `handleSort` function (line 48) sets `setPage(0)` unconditionally. No toast, banner, or focus management accompanies the reset.
**Fix:** Add a brief status announcement (`"Table sorted by {col.label}, reset to page 1"`) via `aria-live`. Consider preserving the user's current page if data exists there, or add a confirmation step for destructive pagination resets.
```

---

## Step 6 — Compile the summary

## Perspective Audit Summary

**Component/artifact reviewed:** SortableTable (Data Table With Sortable Columns and Broken ARIA Sort)
**Perspectives escalated for deep review:** Keyboard & Motor Access, Screen Reader & Semantic Structure, Cognitive & Neurodivergent
**Perspectives at LOW (not reviewed):** Magnification & Reflow, Environmental Contrast, Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity, Auditory Access

### Findings by Severity

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| CRITICAL | 1 |
| MAJOR | 3 |
| MINOR | 1 |
| ENHANCEMENT | 0 |

### Perspectives That Passed

- **Keyboard & Motor Access**: Core keyboard operability, focus visibility, target sizing, and up-event activation all PASS. Only impacted by the missing `aria-sort` (routed to Screen Reader/Semantic).
- **Cognitive & Neurodivergent**: Layout predictability, visual hierarchy, and plain language PASS. One MINOR finding regarding pagination reset behavior.

### Perspectives With Findings — Grouped by ARRM Role

**Front-End Dev**
- Table rows/cells use `<div>` instead of semantic table elements — Screen Reader Semantic — CRITICAL — 1.3.1, 4.1.2
- Sort buttons lack `aria-sort` attribute — Screen Reader Semantic — MAJOR — 4.1.2
- Table updates not announced via `aria-live` or focus management — Screen Reader Semantic — MAJOR — 4.1.3, 2.4.3

**Content Author**
- Pagination links use bare numbers without contextual labels — Screen Reader Semantic — MAJOR — 2.4.4

**UX Design**
- Sorting silently resets pagination to page 0 without warning — Cognitive Neurodivergent — MINOR — 3.2.1, 3.3.4

### Open Questions Requiring Human Verification

- [Human verification required] Confirm whether the component is intended to support full keyboard-only table navigation (arrow keys for cell movement) or if header/button-only interaction is acceptable per product spec.
- [Human verification required] Verify that `aria-live` region placement does not conflict with existing global status/toast systems in the host application.

### Recommended Next Step

**REVISE** — MAJOR findings present (missing semantic table structure, ambiguous pagination link text, unannounced state changes). Address before shipping. CRITICAL finding (div-based table structure) must be resolved to enable screen reader table navigation and column header recognition.
